tasks.short: Trace delayed shipments and coordinate recovery with warehouse, sales, production and carriers.

steps.what: Check the order, promised date and customer requirements.
Check warehouse progress and carrier tracking for the latest shipment event.
Email the responsible team or carrier for missing shipment details.

loop.input: Order context, timestamped shipment events and the unresolved information gap.
loop.output: A short status request with shipment references and specific questions.
loop.check: Verify references and recipient; the clerk approves wording before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per request; missing references return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles standard gaps; unusual shipment histories need a short contextual explanation.

steps.what: Discuss constraints and negotiate feasible recovery options with the responsible people.
Approve a recovery option requiring extra cost or changed shipping commitments.
Record the agreed recovery plan and next follow-up date against the order.

tasks.design: Combine order context from the {ERP} with timestamped events from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {PARTNER_PORTAL} in one exception view. A bounded drafting loop prepares unusual status requests in the {EMAIL}; people negotiate recovery and approve changed commitments. The {WORKFLOW} records the approved plan and schedules follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shipment references and event meanings differ across systems. Recovery also depends on people accepting changed priorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Available interfaces and configurable exception views can remove repeated lookups. AI coding can shorten connector development, while bounded drafting handles unusual explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Stale carrier events, missing scans and scarce production capacity. Software cannot make another team accept a recovery plan.
tasks.human_edge: Know whom to call, test whether a promise is credible and negotiate a workable compromise.

ambition.what: Reprioritise shipment recovery each morning and afternoon using verified delay and customer-impact signals.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling status and more time resolving contested shipments. They can prioritise the recovery queue; spending and changed shipping commitments retain supervisor approval.

reach.task: Recommend which delayed customer orders deserve account-level intervention.
reach.learn: Customer commitments, account priorities and the commercial cost of delay.

evidence.claim: Joining order and shipment events by stable references can remove repeated status lookups.
Rossum documents order validation and exception routing; this supports order-context preparation, not autonomous shipment recovery.
Cross-team recovery negotiation remains dependent on operational constraints and human commitments.

assumptions: The typical setting has an {ERP}, an {OPS_SYSTEM} and carrier tracking through a {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Time shares are illustrative estimates, informed by the coordination-heavy priors.
Build ranges cover one order flow and a small carrier set, including access, rollout and consultation assessment.
GDPR applies to contact and shipment data; employee consultation depends on national rules and the proposed monitoring.
unknowns: Which carrier interfaces and stable shipment identifiers are available?
Who may approve extra freight cost or change a delivery commitment?
Does the proposed exception view require employee consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Which missing shipment events account for most follow-up effort?
Can configured exception views cover the main gaps before custom connectors are built?
new_work: Review drafted status requests before sending.
Investigate stale events and unmatched shipment references.
Maintain carrier mappings, escalation contacts and follow-up rules.

tasks.short: Route approved orders to the departments that prepare and ship them.

steps.what: Check order approval, destination, stock allocation and dispatch requirements.
Resolve blocked releases, special handling or competing dispatch priorities.
Create preparation instructions identifying quantities, destination, handling and responsible department.
Email departments that the dispatch instruction is ready.
Check that the responsible department has accepted the preparation work.

tasks.design: Configure release checks in the {ERP} and route eligible orders into departmental queues in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Queue assignment replaces duplicate {EMAIL} notifications, while the {WORKFLOW} escalates unaccepted work. Blocked releases and competing priorities go to the shipping supervisor before instructions take effect.
tasks.previous_blocker: Release conditions and departmental responsibilities were inconsistently configured. Email compensated for gaps in queue ownership.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing release rules and work queues may already cover most cases. AI-assisted configuration and connector development reduce implementation effort without requiring a model at runtime.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting priorities, unusual destinations and special handling need clear operational authority.
tasks.human_edge: Balance urgent orders against capacity and understand when a technically valid release would disrupt operations.

ambition.what: Provide sales representatives with a pre-release split-shipment proposal for constrained orders.

tasks.altitude: The clerk monitors blocked and unaccepted work instead of repeatedly routing routine orders. They gain queue-triage responsibility; approval of exceptional releases stays with the shipping supervisor.

reach.task: Coordinate customer order priorities with available dispatch capacity.
reach.learn: Release cut-offs, warehouse capacity and the effect of split shipments on customer promises.

evidence.claim: Exact documents order imports and stock synchronisation, supporting structured order handoffs.
Configured release rules and departmental queues can handle routine preparation instructions without a model.
The estimated gain is greater than the human-heavy prior where orders are already approved and release rules are explicit.

assumptions: Most orders have structured quantities, destinations and handling requirements.
Exception discussion is averaged across the workload; not every order requires it.
The {OPS_SYSTEM} supports departmental queues and acceptance status.
Build ranges include permissions, rollout and assessment of consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which release checks are already configured?
Can departments reliably work from assigned queues?
Which order categories require explicit release approval?
Do changed work allocation or monitoring arrangements require employee consultation?
research_questions: How much duplicate notification exists after queue assignment?
Which exceptions genuinely require a supervisor rather than another configured release condition?
new_work: Maintain release conditions and departmental routing.
Investigate orders stuck between assignment and acceptance.
Review exception reasons after operational changes.

tasks.short: Update inventory records from product movements and resolve unsupported adjustments.

steps.what: Retrieve recorded receipts, transfers, dispatches and returns.
Match movement references, quantities and units against current inventory records.
Ask warehouse personnel to explain missing or inconsistent movement evidence.
Approve a correction where normal movement evidence does not support the change.
Post validated movements and approved corrections to inventory.
Check that stock quantities agree with the corresponding financial inventory records.

tasks.design: Configure event-based stock posting in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, using unique movement references to prevent duplicate entries. A deterministic reconciliation compares quantities with the {ERP} and sends discrepancies to an exception queue. Unsupported corrections require inventory-controller approval before posting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Missing movement references, inconsistent units and disconnected stock records made automatic posting unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing stock-posting features and deterministic reconciliation cover the structured work. AI coding can speed mapping and validation development; no model is needed to calculate stock.
tasks.still_hard: Physical movement may differ from recorded movement. Historical errors, bundles, returns and unit conversions need reliable evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Establish what physically happened and distinguish a recording error from a real stock loss.

ambition.what: Prioritise same-day inventory discrepancies by their impact on open customer orders.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time posting movements and more time gathering evidence for stock exceptions. They can prioritise investigations; authority to approve unsupported stock corrections does not change.

reach.task: Check stock confidence before promising a rush-order delivery.
reach.learn: Available-to-promise quantities, inventory holds and the distinction between recorded and verified stock.

evidence.claim: Exact documents stock synchronisation alongside order management.
Reference-based duplicate checks, unit conversion and quantity reconciliation are deterministic operations.
Automating postings does not establish whether an unrecorded physical movement occurred.

assumptions: Routine product movements already create structured events in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
The financial inventory record is held separately in the {ERP}; a shared ledger would eliminate reconciliation.
Investigation and approval shares are workload averages across routine and exceptional movements.
Build ranges include access, stock-control validation, rollout and consultation assessment under national rules.
unknowns: Are stock and financial inventory already maintained in one ledger?
Which movements still rely on paper evidence?
Are movement identifiers, units and reversal rules consistent?
Who may approve stock corrections and at what thresholds?
research_questions: Can existing event-posting settings eliminate manual adjustments before adding an integration?
Which discrepancy categories most often block customer orders?
new_work: Monitor failed, duplicate and out-of-sequence events.
Maintain item mappings, unit conversions and reversal rules.
Investigate reconciliation exceptions and retain correction evidence.

tasks.short: Collect order payments, record receipts and forward any physical tender for processing.

steps.what: Send the customer an approved payment request with the order reference.
Check received funds against the payment request using settled bank transactions.
Resolve ambiguous allocations, short payments or unidentified receipts.
Record the receipt and allocate it to the order or invoice.
Send a receipt confirming the amount received and any remaining balance.
Where accepted, hand physical tender and its custody record to finance for processing.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to issue payment requests and receipts from approved invoice data, and connect settled {BANK} transactions for deterministic matching. Exact matches post automatically; ambiguous allocations require finance approval. Physical tender retains a recorded human custody handoff where it is still accepted.
tasks.previous_blocker: Missing payment references, delayed bank imports and separate receipt records required repeated checks and rekeying.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured receipt workflows and bank interfaces can cover routine collection without a model. AI coding can reduce the effort needed for mapping, duplicate checks and exception views.
tasks.still_hard: Combined payments, partial settlements, unidentified senders and physical custody. Settlement and invoice allocation must remain distinct.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve disputed balances fairly and establish who paid for which obligation when references are ambiguous.

ambition.what: Prioritise unresolved receipts before each dispatch cut-off to prevent avoidable prepaid-order holds.

tasks.altitude: The clerk handles payment exceptions and customer explanations instead of copying receipts between screens. They can prioritise payment investigations; finance retains authority over ambiguous allocations.

reach.task: Help a first-time customer complete prepaid-order payment setup.
reach.learn: Customer identity checks, payment references, settlement timing and escalation routes.

evidence.claim: Structured payment-reference matching, duplicate detection and receipt generation can use deterministic rules.
Electronic payment evidence does not replace physical custody where physical tender remains accepted.
The human-heavy prior overstates routine handling where bank settlement and invoice references are structured.
GDPR applies where payment records contain personal data.

assumptions: Electronic payment predominates in this illustrative European setting; physical tender is a small conditional branch.
Time shares measure staff effort, excluding customer payment time and passive waiting.
Automatic matching requires a unique reference, consistent currency and amount, and no conflicting allocation.
Customer receipts use approved templates and confirmed postings; no model sees payment credentials.
Build ranges include restricted bank access, finance validation, rollout and consultation assessment under national rules.
unknowns: Which payment methods and physical instruments are actually accepted?
Does the {ERP} already provide bank matching and automatic receipts?
Which settlement events are authoritative for each payment method?
Who approves ambiguous allocations and payment-related order holds?
research_questions: What share of receipts can existing matching settings allocate uniquely?
Which payment exceptions cause the most avoidable dispatch delays?
new_work: Review unmatched receipts and conflicting allocations.
Monitor bank-import failures and duplicate receipt prevention.
Maintain matching rules, settlement mappings and receipt templates.
Retain physical custody records where needed.

role.altitude: The order clerk becomes an exception coordinator across order release, shipment recovery, inventory confidence and payment readiness. Routine records move automatically; authority over spending, unsupported stock corrections and ambiguous payment allocations stays with the relevant approvers.
reach: Sales representatives: assess the customer impact of shipment and stock exceptions.
First-line sales supervisors: align dispatch priorities with operational capacity.
New accounts clerks: help first-time buyers complete prepaid-order setup.
skills_to_grow: Trace an order across operational and financial records.
Distinguish confirmed events from estimates and missing evidence.
Diagnose reference, unit and allocation mismatches.
Negotiate recovery options and explain customer trade-offs.
Maintain exception rules and validate changes with process owners.
role.ambitious_version: Run a daily order-readiness service that identifies stock, payment and dispatch blockers before customer promises fail, with named owners and evidence for each intervention.
